quiz.q: What does Rust's concurrency motto "share memory by communicating" mean in practice?
options: Threads should share a global mutable variable
Threads pass ownership of values through a channel instead of reaching into shared memory
Only `main` is allowed to hold any data
Every value must be wrapped in `unsafe`
quiz.explain: Instead of multiple threads touching the same memory, one thread sends a value down a channel and the other receives full ownership of it — no shared mutable state involved.

quiz.q: What does `mpsc` stand for, and what does it mean for `Receiver`?
options: Multi-producer, single-consumer — there's only ever one `Receiver`
Multi-process shared cache — receivers can be cloned freely
Message-passing sync channel — it's always bounded
Multi-consumer, single-producer — only one thread may ever send
quiz.explain: `mpsc::channel()` supports many producers (clone `Sender` as needed) but exactly one consumer — `Receiver` is not `Clone`.

quiz.q: After `tx.send(value)`, what can the sending thread still do with `value`?
options: Read it, but not mutate it
Nothing — `send` takes ownership, so `value` was moved
Clone it for free since channels borrow internally
Send it again on the same channel
quiz.explain: `Sender::send(&self, t: T)` takes `T` by value. Once sent, the value belongs to the receiving thread; using it again on the sender's side is a use-after-move error.

quiz.q: You need three threads to all send messages into one channel. What do you do?
options: Clone the `Receiver` three times
Clone the `Sender` once per thread — each clone is a handle to the same pipe
Create three separate `mpsc::channel()` pairs and merge them manually
Wrap `tx` in a `Mutex` so threads take turns
quiz.explain: `Sender` implements `Clone` for exactly this reason. Each clone points at the same channel, so many threads can send independently.

quiz.q: When does a `for msg in rx` loop finish?
options: After exactly one message is received
Once every `Sender` (the original plus all clones) has been dropped
As soon as the receiving thread calls `.stop()`
It never finishes automatically — you must `break` manually
quiz.explain: `Receiver` iterates until it's certain no more messages can arrive, which is exactly when every `Sender` handle has gone out of scope.

quiz.q: A `for msg in rx` loop hangs forever even though every worker thread finished. What's the likely cause?
options: The channel is bounded and full
A `Sender` clone (maybe the original `tx`, unused after cloning) is still alive somewhere and was never dropped
`Receiver` requires an explicit `.close()` call
The messages are the wrong type
quiz.explain: As long as any `Sender` handle exists — even one nobody is actively using — the channel isn't considered closed, so the receiving loop keeps waiting.

quiz.q: Why might `.send(value).unwrap()` panic in a long-running producer thread?
options: `send` always fails on the first call
`send` returns `Err` once the `Receiver` has been dropped, and there's nothing left to receive the value
Only `.recv()` can fail, never `.send()`
Sending more than one value always errors
quiz.explain: If the reader gave up and dropped `rx`, `send` returns `Err(SendError(value))` handing the value back. Unwrapping that panics — worth handling explicitly in long-lived producers.

flashcards.back: `let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();` — `tx` is the `Sender`, `rx` is the `Receiver`.
Moves it across the channel — the receiving thread gets ownership, not a reference.

flashcards.front: How do multiple threads send into one channel?
flashcards.back: Clone the `Sender` (`tx.clone()`) once per thread — each clone is a handle to the same underlying pipe.

flashcards.front: When does `for msg in rx` stop looping?
flashcards.back: Automatically, once every `Sender` (original and all clones) has been dropped — no manual close needed.

flashcards.front: Why does an unused `Sender` clone left alive cause a hang?
flashcards.back: The channel only closes once ALL senders are gone. One forgotten clone (even idle) keeps the receiver waiting forever.
No — only `Sender` is `Clone`. `std::sync::mpsc` always has exactly one consumer.
